brief.scope: First independent review of the three Grok startup/enforcement test files at the corrected candidate. No runtime inspection/edit. Verify exact declared bootstrap, pure prepare, native normalization, config refusal, actual-client observation, opaque role/target custody, lifecycle, resume and six-axis controls. Reproduce 96/112 assertion-red, hashes, registered lint and custody. Treat the producer's three admitted invented/incomplete fixture schemas as real acceptance questions: a conforming loader must not be forced to allow undeclared delegate/board JSON or incomplete transport. Existing startup contract review has unresolved identity, binding and FD6 couplings; classify test versus contract ownership without inventing a positive or freezing guesses. Return APPROVE/CHANGES and precise bounded remedies. No full floor, live vendor/settings/state or source changes.

findings.claim: The actual-client MCP gate is unsatisfiable by any conforming implementation. invoke_conduct -> run_cli spawns a subprocess (support.py:1785 `[sys.executable, "-B", str(self.cli_entry), *argv]`), and the only channel to that child is FD 3-8 sealed slots plus env (support.py:983-997, 1740-1775). FakeMcpClient is a plain in-process Python object in the parent test process; nothing writes to it from the child, and the launcher-created anonymous observation pipe the contract requires (conductor-start-plan.md:522-540: write end in the server, read end in the canonical supervisor) is never created anywhere in the fixture (the only os.pipe call is support.py:842, the malformed-slot 'pipe' kind). Yet test_harness_dev_is_an_admitted_form asserts `self.assertTrue(self.mcp_client.observations)` and assert_connection_observations after the subprocess returns. A correct conduct.py exits 0 and leaves self.mcp_client.observations == [], so the positive fails forever. This is the exact defect correction row conductor-start-plan.md:649 named ('FakeMcpClient must act as the client child on the bound server pipes'); it was renamed, not fixed.
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'os.pipe\|observations' ops/conductor/tests/conduct_test_support.py | sed -n '1,40p'  -> the only os.pipe is line 842 inside SealedBootstrap.open; FakeMcpClient.emit_connection (594-664) is only ever called in-process by the parent. sed -n '1777,1820p' ops/conductor/tests/conduct_test_support.py shows run_cli/invoke_conduct is subprocess.run with pass_fds only. sed -n '77,90p' ops/conductor/tests/test_conduct_start.py shows the assertion on the parent-side object.

findings.claim: The FD 6 transport slot conforms to no declared shape, so a conforming loader must refuse every positive fixture. conductor-start-plan.md:373-374 requires each slot to obey its owning strict schema. The two candidate owners are the trusted compilation transport handle, exactly {executable,configuration,manifest,canonical_paths,evidence,launch_session,resume,relay} (harness-capabilities.md:131-142), and transport.relay, exactly {schema,processes,endpoint,configuration,rpc,targets,deadlines,resume} with schema codex-relay/1 (harness-capabilities.md:452-454, all keys required). slot_bytes emits {mechanism,executable,grammar,interception,relay} with relay={'schema':'codex-relay/1'} only. Three keys (mechanism, grammar, interception) are declared nowhere; configuration, manifest, canonical_paths, evidence and launch_session are absent, and the relay object is missing seven of its eight required members. Consequences are concrete, not stylistic: descriptor.mcp.catalogue_sha256 and server_sha256 come from configuration.mcp, descriptor.adapter.normalizer_sha256 from manifest.adapter, launch_id from launch_session (conductor-start-plan.md:456-460), and the delegate/read target declarations from relay.targets — none has a held source in the six slots, while test_catalogue_has_eleven_v3_tools:726-729 asserts descriptor.mcp.catalogue_sha256 == canonical_digest(self.catalogue) exactly. The prior startup review flagged FD 6 as ambiguous (P3-1); the tests answered with a third shape matching neither reading.

findings.claim: test_compound_command_naming_dispatch_is_not_an_allowed_request applies the withdrawn behaviour the correction explicitly deleted. It builds a native RPC frame {'id':7,'method':'command/exec','params':{...}} via relay_rpc and passes it to normalize_tool, then requires a closed conductor-tool/1 Request with kind 'forbidden', target 'implementation', reason 'shell-escape'. permission-surface.md:143 states 'Framing and correlation run first in the relay; no jsonrpc wrapper enters normalize_tool'; :147 states TUI command/exec receives its declared terminal disposition at the relay gate and is 'not invented dynamic calls or shell Requests'; :350 fixes that disposition as error -32601. The correction row at permission-surface.md:274 says verbatim: 'Assert its prescribed terminal error/refusal and zero canonical invocations; do not require a fabricated forbidden/shell-escape Request from an unsupported protocol.' The second half (lines 494-502) has the same defect: an undeclared argument on a declared dynamic target must refuse before execution (permission-surface.md:401-405), while the test requires assert_closed_object(bad, REQUEST_KEYS) — a Request object, not a refusal.

Two tests demand opposite exit codes for byte-identical child input. FaultyControls.test_malformed_hook_payload_prevents_admission builds `live = self.make_context(mechanism=MECHANISM_CODEX)` with no fault injected, invokes ['codex','dev'] and asserts `assertIn(proc.returncode, (2, 3))`. CliForms.test_harness_dev_is_an_admitted_form builds the identical context with the identical call and asserts `assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0)`. The child sees only the six sealed slot buffers and the env map, which are byte-identical in both cases, so no implementation can satisfy both. Correction row conductor-start-plan.md:676 asked for live malformed payload injection at the admitted mechanism's interceptor after child creation; the test injects nothing into the live arm.

findings.claim: Purity is measured cumulatively from the setUp baseline, not across the call under test, so every test that legitimately launches and then calls prepare is self-contradictory. EffectsLog.capture() runs once in setUp (line 965); delta() compares against that single baseline forever; assert_no_durable_effects fails if any added path ends with record.json or contains /attempts/, and also asserts self.dispatch.claimed_path is None and not self.receipt.exists(). But retained_descriptor (1829-1837) requires a record.json to exist under self.root after a successful canonical launch. So in test_harness_prod_is_an_admitted_form the successful invoke_conduct at line 95 must write record.json, and the assert_prepare_ok at line 100 must then find no record.json in added. Strictly contradictory. Same pattern: test_double_dash_may_carry_zero_tokens (106 then 111), test_tokens_after_double_dash_are_forwarded_in_order (117 then 128), McpConnection.test_actual_client_must_initialize_list_and_call_lane_start (596 then 603), Onboarding.test_resume_reverifies_the_actual_client_connection (805/818 then 839), Onboarding.test_changed_discovery_content_does_not_change_bound_profile (869/891 then 911, which additionally requires claimed_path is None after two canonical claims).

The FD 3-8 relocation is defeated by CPython's child_exec ordering and only works by accident. _spawn passes the raw memfd numbers in pass_fds and relocates them to 3-8 inside preexec_fn; CPython runs preexec_fn before _close_open_fds(3, fds_to_keep), and fds_to_keep contains the original numbers, not the relocated destinations. Measured on this host: when the six memfds land on 3-8 the relocation is a no-op and the child reads all six slots; when they land on 9-14 the child gets EBADF on every one of 3-8. So bootstrap delivery depends on the parent process's open-fd state (a runner, plugin or leftover handle shifts it) and silently degrades every CLI positive into a bootstrap-missing refusal that looks like an implementation defect. Bounded remedy: dup the slots onto 3-8 in the parent and pass those numbers in pass_fds, or add range(3,9) to pass_fds.

Both scripts replicate conduct_test_support.py:1740-1775 verbatim.

findings.claim: The trusted context is an undeclared fixture protocol carrying fixture objects and boolean fault switches as prepare authority — the SimpleNamespace pattern renamed, not removed. conductor-start-plan.md:330 says trusted_context 'contains the policy owner's verified binding, declaration sources, custody anchor and discovery boot inputs' and declares no member interface. TrustedContext.get(name) with fixture-chosen keys is invented, and make_context puts self.dispatch, self.effects, self.mcp_client and self.mcp_server into it, plus the booleans candidate_origin and interception. A conforming prepare_conductor must therefore read undeclared keys to reserve the launch id, to obtain the catalogue, and to decide bootstrap-untrusted and the interception refusal. Correction row conductor-start-plan.md:639 required the trusted fixture binder and owner-verified evidence rather than authority switches; row 677 said a fixture manifest flag is insufficient provenance. Bounded remedy: derive every prepare input from the six sealed slot buffers, and inject faults by changing those bytes, not by setting context booleans.

COND-AXIS-N1 asserts the wrong refusal class on the profile axis and contradicts its own sibling. test_cond_axis_n1_each_axis_conflict_refuses_without_substitution loops all six LaunchSelection members and asserts class 'lane-policy' for every one, including profile='prod' against a held base of profile='dev'. lane-policy.md:222-223 declares 'Empty, unknown, malformed or conflicting selection refuses lane-profile before a child starts'; the class table at :687 assigns 'missing, empty, unknown or conflicting profile selection' to lane-profile; N1 at :773 repeats it; the walkthrough at :632 says a profile conflict returns its owning refusal. test_profile_must_exist_in_policy_and_discovery (start:264-269) correctly asserts lane-profile for the same axis, so a conforming evaluator cannot satisfy both. Bounded remedy: expect lane-profile for the profile subTest, lane-policy for the other five.

The missing-interception refusal class is frozen on a guess and the planted fault is still a manifest flag. harness-capabilities.md contains zero refusal lines (grep -c 'expected .*; found .*; needed' returns 0) and states only that a missing required interceptor 'makes that harness/operation unavailable for conduct' (:281-286); conductor-start-plan.md:588 defers capability failures to 'their owner's refusal', which no owner declares. The tests assert 'lane-policy', whose declared condition is 'invalid/untrusted/missing authority, binding or declarations' (lane-policy.md:688) — not capability evidence; lane-dependency (:690, 'unresolved required dependency evidence') is at least as good a reading. Separately, correction row conductor-start-plan.md:677 said to remove required mechanism/closure evidence from trusted transport because 'A fixture manifest flag is insufficient provenance'; interception=False is still exactly a manifest flag, written into transport.json as an undeclared boolean member (support.py:1606). Bounded remedy: name the capability class in its owner, and inject the fault by removing declared mechanism/closure members rather than flipping a boolean.

findings.claim: make_catalogue does not supply the eleven owner schemas, contrary to correction row conductor-start-plan.md:648 and the producer's own note. Measured against ops/conductor/tools/lane_mcp.py:_schemas at this ref: lane_alerts drops both declared 'default' members ('after' default 0, 'limit' default 5, lane_mcp.py:86-89); lane_start drops the cursor pattern '^[0-9a-f]{64}:(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,2})$'; lane_homes drops the concept pattern '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$' and the cursor pattern; lane_handoffs drops the key pattern '^record/[0-9a-f]{64}$' and the cursor pattern (lane_mcp.py:147-155). Five of eleven schemas differ. V3_TOOL_NAMES order is also wrong: the owner emits lane_brief, lane_record, lane_alerts, lane_usage, then findings/changes/jobs, then DISCOVERY_QUERIES = lane_start, lane_homes, lane_handoffs, lane_actions (lane_read.py:1522); the fixture leads with lane_record, lane_alerts, lane_usage, lane_brief, and assert_connection_observations:1977 asserts ordered equality. The catalogue digest is descriptor.mcp.catalogue_sha256, so this is a shape obligation on a verified mock, not cosmetic.

Six of the eight EffectsLog counters are write-only fixture state that nothing under test can ever increment, so the purity and zero-invocation assertions built on them are vacuous. executor_calls is appended only by FakeDispatch.reserve/claim (support.py:555,564); prompts, children, hooks, transport_writes and mcp_calls are appended by nothing at all in the three files. assert_no_durable_effects (1843-1846) and assert_prepare_pure (1858-1863) therefore assert five constants. The same emptiness carries the load in test_replayed_binding_prevents_admission:720-723 ('zero second invocation'), test_binding_mismatch_is_refused:618, test_adapter_cannot_turn_refusal_into_a_prompt:677-678 and test_compound_command...:493. Correction row conductor-start-plan.md:642 required the effects log to observe the canonical executor's calls; only the record-bytes half (record_paths/claimed_record) was implemented.

findings.claim: The 'missing FD 3' case required by correction row conductor-start-plan.md:664 is not tested. SealedBootstrap.open skips absent slots and appends the survivors contiguously, and _spawn's relocate enumerates from FD 3, so missing_slots=('custody.json',) delivers declarations.json at FD 3, binding.json at FD 4 ... and leaves FD 8 unpopulated. The planted fault is a missing FD 8 plus five mis-slotted buffers, not a missing FD 3. The assertion still passes only because conduct-config checks missing before invalid (conductor-start-plan.md:581-585), so the shifted-content fault is never exercised. Bounded remedy: leave a hole at the removed slot's own descriptor number instead of compacting.

The unresolved DispatchID producer question is settled by fixture fiat rather than reported. The prior startup-coupling review raised it as P2 (slot 5 seals a ConductorBinding whose dispatch member is the reserved id, while conductor-start-plan.md:323-324,415,438 put the reservation inside the preflight and lane-policy.md:632 makes ConductorBinding a policy derivation from startup-supplied inputs). Measured here: conductor-start-plan.md and permission-surface.md are byte-identical between 6bf5d7b and d3b9588 (git diff --stat over those paths is empty; sha256 7b79701f... and f77611d6... match the prior review's), so the gap is still open. make_context calls self.dispatch.reserve() before sealing binding.json and test_launch_id_is_reserved_in_memory_before_admission asserts desc['launch_id'] == self.dispatch.reserved, adopting the pre-sealed reading and reaching the reservation object through the undeclared context key 'dispatch'. The brief asked for classification without freezing a guess; this freezes one. Bounded remedy: keep the assertion on the DispatchID grammar and the sealed-binding equality, and record the producer question as a declared unresolved edge instead of binding the implementation to a fixture object.

findings.claim: The conduct-config reason 'input-mismatch' is asserted to exist in the closed set but never exercised. grep -c 'input-mismatch' returns 1 in test_conduct_start.py (the tuple assertion) and 0 in test_conduct_enforcement.py. Its declared trigger is stated exactly at conductor-start-plan.md:584-585 ('otherwise differing held transport bytes select input-mismatch'), which is directly constructible: seal transport bytes at FD 6 that differ from the held copy. Four of the five reasons have cases; the fifth is a declared gap that is not declared.

The declared role-handle lookup cannot be driven from the declared native call, and the tests silently pick a resolution strategy. permission-surface.md:109 declares resolve_tool(kind, target) with 'exact lookup in already admitted owner declarations, no wildcard/default', while DynamicToolCallParams carries only namespace and tool (:396-398) and the relay is told to 'derive kind/target from that row' (:407). No declared member maps a tool name to its kind; relay.targets does carry kind (harness-capabilities.md:459) but the fixture transport omits targets entirely (see the FD 6 finding). test_read_containing_apply_is_not_classified_as_mutation therefore requires normalize_tool to return kind='read', target='board' from tool='board' with no declared route. Ownership: this is a permission-surface gap, not a test defect; the tests should record it as unresolved rather than assume enumeration over kinds.

The producer's two admitted invented fixture schemas (delegate dispatch/go/ladder, board read section/json/offline) are real but contained, and the containment should be stated rather than left implicit. Because the argument schema lives on the opaque BoundTarget minted by the fixture binder (permission-surface.md:112-123,129), a conforming evaluate_tool validates arguments against handle.schema and never embeds the invented key sets, so no undeclared JSON is forced on the implementation. What is not contained: the declared source of a target declaration is relay.targets, 'sorted unique array of {namespace,tool,kind,target,declaration:{path,sha256}}' with 'no undeclared target is synthesized' (harness-capabilities.md:459), and target_handle instead fabricates declaration={'path':'fixture/<kind>/<target>.json', ref, sha256} outside that member, while effects={'writes':[]} carries no operation identity or reconciliation support — permission-surface.md:486 makes such a lever 'unavailable as an effectful target', and :283-287 forbids fabricating a positive target on exactly those grounds. Bounded remedy: route fixture target rows through a relay.targets member in the FD 6 slot and mark the delegate/board argument schemas as an unavailable edge until their frontend owners declare them.

The binding-mismatch Request-versus-held gap is still open and correction row permission-surface.md:277 remains unsatisfiable as written; the tests were right not to freeze it, and that should be recorded as a declared gap rather than left silent. permission-surface.md:217 ('The id/binding must match Request and the held current binding') is byte-identical at 6bf5d7b and d3b9588, so the prior review's P2 stands. Row :277 instructs the test owner to 'Assert the exact fixed binding-mismatch/malformed-request Decision', but the contract still does not say which digest Decision.binding_sha256 carries when Request and held binding differ. test_binding_mismatch_is_refused asserts only the closed key set, outcome refuse and refusal.found; it makes no digest claim. Correct choice, undeclared.

envelope.note:
Verdict: changes, at d3b9588e10a10ef356e87a385cfd16490b09bb92 against 710dbac38c3b187eb4b3302308430c0a6dec4d76. Read-only: nothing in the snapshot was edited; scratch went to out/ only; no runtime inspection of absent implementations, no live vendor, settings or state, no full floor.

Reproduction is exact. All three original hashes at 3980c3b, all three corrected hashes at d3b9588, and all three red counts (54/59, 42/53, 96/112, zero errors) match the producer's receipts. ruff check and ruff format --check are clean on the three files. git status is empty before and after. Custody holds: contracts by GPT-6, tests by Grok 4.6, this review by Claude Opus 5, no producer owning consecutive artifacts. The reds are assertion failures against absent source, not collection errors, as claimed.

The corrections that were asked for were largely made. Bootstrap is FD 3-8 sealed anonymous memfds with the declared seals, sizes and deadline constants; prepare packaging is exactly {descriptor,compiled_launch} with the tuple, list and compiled aliases gone; assert_prepare_refused now demands a refusal-wire string with no trailing newline; native input is the six DynamicToolCallParams members with PIN_NATIVE_REQUEST removed; the conduct-config line and its five-reason enum, the conduct-mcp line, and the conduct-argv line with its index-0 vector rule are byte-exact against their owners; BoundRole and BoundTarget are opaque immutable handles with the declared operations and views; COND-AXIS-N1 now conflicts all six members including effort; Codex keeps empty grammar and is permitted identical resume argv; late MCP failure asserts Abort 3 with result.status invalid, envelope null and retained policy. The conduct-observations/1 report keys are exactly the eleven declared fields.

What blocks acceptance is five ways the suite cannot be satisfied by any conforming implementation, not a matter of degree. First, the actual-client MCP gate: invoke_conduct spawns a subprocess whose only channel is the six sealed buffers and the environment, FakeMcpClient is an in-process parent object, and the launcher-created observation pipe the contract requires is never created anywhere in the fixture, yet thirteen positives assert that the child populated mcp_client.observations. Second, FD 6: transport.json is {mechanism,executable,grammar,interception,relay} with relay carrying one of its eight required members, which matches neither the eight-member compilation transport nor the eight-member codex-relay/1 object, so a loader obeying conductor-start-plan.md:373 must refuse every positive; descriptor.mcp.catalogue_sha256, server_sha256, adapter.normalizer_sha256 and the target declarations then have no held source. Third, the compound-command test feeds a JSON-RPC frame into normalize_tool and demands a shell-escape Request, which is exactly what permission-surface.md:274 told the test owner to remove and what :143,:147 and :350 forbid. Fourth, FaultyControls and CliForms demand exit 2-or-3 and exit 0 for byte-identical child input. Fifth, purity is measured cumulatively from the setUp baseline, so any test that launches and then prepares contradicts itself.

One measured operational defect worth fixing regardless of the above: the FD relocation in _spawn is defeated by CPython closing descriptors after preexec_fn. Measured on this host, slots landing on 3-8 work and slots landing on 9-14 give the child EBADF on all six, so bootstrap delivery depends on the parent's open-fd state and would silently degrade every CLI positive into a bootstrap-missing refusal that reads as an implementation defect. The remedy is one line: include the destination descriptors in pass_fds.

Every finding carries a bounded remedy. None requires reopening a frozen boundary, and none is an instruction to admit runtime, approve a contract or run a floor.
